help.title: Pairing help
help.intro: PocketShell needs a small host agent on the computer you want to control. These are the parts that matter before you install it.
help.install.title: Why install an agent?
help.install.body: The phone app cannot open a terminal by itself. The PocketShell agent runs on a computer you own, keeps an outbound connection to PocketShell, and starts the local daemon after pairing.
help.approval.title: Why scan a QR?
help.approval.body: Running pocketshell pair shows a one-time QR. This phone is trusted only after you scan that QR and approve the host inside the app.
help.access.title: What can it access?
help.access.body: After pairing, approved devices can request terminal sessions and host features exposed by the agent. PocketShell does not open public inbound ports on your computer.
help.transport.title: How does traffic move?
help.transport.body: The backend handles account, pairing, and signaling. Session data prefers WebRTC between your phone and host, and can use TURN relay when direct connectivity is unavailable.
help.camera.title: Camera permission blocked?
help.camera.body: Open device settings and allow Camera for PocketShell, or sign in on another phone or tablet and scan the QR from there.
help.remove.title: How do I remove it?
help.remove.body: Run pocketshell uninstall on the host to stop the daemon, remove the service, clear local PocketShell state, and remove the agent binary.
help.footnote: Only pair computers you own or are authorized to access.
